Method of Attack: Generates login screens overlaid on banking and crypto exchange apps' login forms to steal credentials via phishing HTML pages
Emulates Google Protect to request Accessibility Service permissions to perform malicious actions
Abuses Accessibility Service to prevent removal, exfiltrate Google Authenticator OTPs, process commands, and steal PIN/password fields
Exfiltrates list of installed apps to receive matching fake HTML login form injections from C2 server
Generates fake notifications to lure victims to phishing pages
Uses screen recording to capture credentials for apps not on the target list

Executes commands from C2 with administrator privileges including USSD requests, SMS sending, app launching, cache cleaning, call forwarding, opening browsers, SOCKS5 proxy control, self-deletion, and push notifications
Feature modules include keylogging, VNC server launching, screen recording, screen locking, notification exfiltration and blocking, silent mode, WebSocket connection, and screen dimming
Impacted Systems: Banking apps (215 apps targeted, including in US, Turkey, Spain, Canada, France, Germany, UK)
Attack Vector: Unknown initial infection method; limited distribution found in Google Play Store apps
Malicious apps mimicking popular apps (e.g., a music tool in Turkey)
Indicators of Compromise: Fake HTML login pages mimicking legitimate apps
Fake notifications leading to phishing pages
Exfiltration of usernames, passwords, Google Authenticator OTPs
Commands from C2 server controlling device functions
Malicious apps previously found on Google Play but now removed
